title: Dynamic legend & tooltip: focus targeting, localization-friendly microcopy prototype
creator: Amina Patel
description: Background: The Cost Explorer and Route Dashboards use compact color legends and hover-only tooltips to explain metric bands and rate tiers. For keyboard-dependent users and users in RTL locales, the existing hover-first approach causes discoverability, focus-targeting and translation problems. Goal: ship a production-ready UI pattern that makes legends and their tooltips reliably accessible by keyboard and screenreader, is resilient in RTL locales, and lets localized microcopy adapt for currency and unit abbreviations without layout breakage. Scope: prototype a unified 'dynamic legend' component with: 1) explicit focus targets for each legend item (>= 24px interactive target), 2) tooltip that can be invoked by keyboard (Enter/Space) and remains visible for screen readers (aria-describedby + role="note" fallback), 3) persistent accessible label area for compact / collapsed legends, 4) locale-aware truncation rules for microcopy (JPY/CNY no decimals, long locale names collapse with ellipsis and accessible full text), and 5) high-contrast color token fallback and a11y color pass for colorblind palettes. Out-of-scope: analytics instrumentation (tracked separately as ENG-4482) and autosuggest of locale-select. Acceptance criteria: - Keyboard: Tab to legend group, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move focus between items, Enter/Space toggles tooltip open and closes on Esc. - Screenreader: Each legend item exposes concise label and expanded description via aria-describedby when tooltip is open; when collapsed the group has an accessible summary node. - Localization: Localized microcopy substitutions do not push layout beyond container width and ellipsized content provides a visible "More" affordance that announces full text to SRs. - Contrast: All color mappings meet contrast ratio >= 3:1 for small UI tokens and >= 4.5:1 for legend text; fallback tokens provided in token map. - Visual: Focus ring and target hit area match platform tokens and are consistent with console density settings. - Performance: Tooltip open/close has no layout shift and is keyboard-responsive under 80ms on standard dev machines. Design decisions and tradeoffs: - Chose toggleable tooltip instead of hover-only to avoid ephemeral SR announcements; tradeoff is extra click for mouse-first users but mitigated by showing a subtle persistent label when space constrained. - We avoid tooltip heavy content; keep expanded descriptions to 2 lines and link to detailed docs for longer explanations. - For RTL we flip tooltip anchor and increase horizontal padding to avoid overlap with scrubber. Implementation notes for engineering: - Provide focusable element with role="button" and aria-expanded; when expanded append a visually-hidden description element referenced by aria-describedby. - Use CSS containment to prevent expensive reflows when toggling tooltip. - Provide a tokenized color palette and a11y fallback tokens via token names: --color-legend-a, --color-legend-a-contrast, etc. - Localization: pass both localizedLabel and localizedLongText; UI should render localizedLongText into the hidden description element for SRs. Deliverables: Figma prototype, a11y test plan (manual + Axe checks), localized microcopy table for 30 locales, engineering handoff spec with CSS token map and ARIA examples.
